newsitem.title: USA: Mattel, Wal-Mart sued over dolls.
newsitem.headline: Mattel, Wal-Mart sued over dolls.

text.p: Attorney George Najjar filed suit against Mattel Inc and Wal-Mart Stores Inc seeking $25 million in punitive damages on behalf of a young girl whose hair was allegedly chewed to the scalp by Mattel's Cabbage Patch Doll.
Najjar said his client, nine-year-old Jessica Wells, awoke screaming on December 29 to find the Cabbage Patch Snacktime Kids Doll had consumed her hair to her scalp.
The suit was filed in San Diego County Court on behalf of Jessica and her mother and stepfather, Tom and Genie Taylor.

"To date we have recieved notification of this one lawsuit related to the Snacktime Kids and we have not yet received that complaint. With that in mind, we are unable to respond to any questions regarding this alleged suit," Mattel said in a statement Friday.
Wal-Mart had no immediate comment. The attorney was not immediately available to cite reasons for naming Wal-Mart in the suit.
The battery operated doll is designed to chew and consume plastic food.

On December 31, Mattel announced it would attach warning labels to the dolls still on store shelves and all future production following dozens of reports of children getting their hands and hair stuck in the dolls' mouths.

This was followed by an announcement on January 6 that Mattel would stop making the dolls, voluntarily withdrew them from retail shelves and offered a $40 refund to anyone who was dissatisfied with the toy.
As of midnight Thursday, Mattel said it had received slightly over 1,000 requests for refunds. Over 500,000 dolls had been sold in the U.S.
